scores.notes: Two near-identical bearded men in the same purple gold-trimmed robe and cap lean over the rim side by side at upper right, so the king is drawn twice and one of them is a prominent figure the text does not call for. Daniel hauled up by rope past calm lions is otherwise right.
A 3x crop of the left edge shows the washes ending at ragged boundaries with cream bare paper beyond, about y 390-500 and in the bottom-left corner; small but visible, and accepted for this item.

The central, largest figure is an old man reading an open scroll aloud to seated women and children: a reciter delivering the genealogy the verse consists of rather than Obed, Jesse or David. Flawed on the agreed scene_mismatch and lettering as well.

The image is fully judgeable: Israelites with staffs and loaded donkeys on the road below a mountain capped with cloud and radiance, no figure for God. Both scorers answered every fault no apart from the accepted unpainted edge, so the verdict follows as acceptable; the foreground walkers facing the mountain is an oddity neither scored as a fault.

Holmes in profile at the window wears a plain black frock coat with slicked-back hair and a briar pipe, generic Victorian dress with nothing that reproduces one screen adaptation's costume or props; the claimed likeness rests on the gaunt face alone. Flawed on the agreed lettering (pseudo-script on slip, newspaper and letters).

A 3x crop shows a segmented blue caterpillar body carrying a fully human old-man face, fingered human hands, a bowler hat and a buttoned waistcoat the text never gives it, which breaks the rule that talking animals are drawn as animals with dress only where the text gives it. The glyphs on the hookah band are the agreed lettering.

The four courtiers flanking the Queen at upper right (man in ruff and red cape, girl in a blue gown, lady in a blue headdress, man in a gold doublet) are ordinary full-bodied humans, not flat oblong cards. At 14x the corner index on the spade card at right is an elongated oval about 6px tall, not a legible 6, so with the pips the marks stay unreadable.

Winged, face-veiled seraphim hover above a cloud of glory in the gold temple with Isaiah looking up from below: the right subject, action and place. Their two-wing forms, cloth veils and bare feet are a creature-form failure already carried by the agreed rule_violation, which makes the item flawed.

On the central throne robe-like drapery falls over a lap-and-knees form with a white-cored blaze where torso and head would sit, giving the Ancient of Days a seated body against the no-human-body rule. Most white at the edges is ink-outlined cloud, but a 5x crop of the right edge shows the washes ending at a pigment line 2-7px short of the edge with paper white beyond (about y 190-270), and unmodelled paper-white cloud runs off the top and right edges.

A 4x crop of the falling Lizard juror at centre shows a green scaly tail, legs and clawed hands but a badger-shaped head with the same black-and-cream facial stripes as the badger jurors beside it, a hybrid malformed face. Small but real; the card pips are the agreed lettering.

Holmes at centre is bareheaded in a plain black frock coat, waistcoat and wing collar with a hat in hand; nothing in costume, hair or props reproduces a specific screen adaptation, and the claimed likeness rests on the gaunt face alone. Hatherley with bandaged hand pointing at the burning house, engines, drive and rose-bushes match the moment; bare paper at lower left is accepted.

Small but measurable: the blue sky wash stops at a visible boundary leaving bare cream paper in the top-left corner and a sliver on the left edge above the wall, and an unwashed band runs to the right edge between the cloud wash and the hill (about y 50-105). Accepted for this item; the father, ragged son and servants with robe and sandals are right.

Two court guards, left of the tart table and large in the right foreground, are ordinary full-bodied humans in red coats and tricorns where the court's soldiers should be flat oblong cards. Zoomed crops show a clear figure 8 as the corner index of the heart card behind the Hatter and marks reading 88 on the Hatter's hat tag, which are numerals rather than pips.

The largest, foreground figure is a grey-bearded elder gesturing outward as if presenting, with a half-unrolled blank scroll on the bench beside him, a family group behind and a Roman soldier down the street. He reads as a narrator presenting the book of the genealogy, not as Jesus, David or Abraham.

Edge crops show the dark wash ending at a ragged boundary with a thin strip of white paper down the right and left edges and a white wedge in the bottom-left corner (the outer columns are 35-45 percent near-white). Accepted for this item; Holmes lashing at the bell-pull with the match lit, snake by the ventilator and Watson on the bed are right.

Corner crops show the floor wash under the side table ending at a ragged boundary with cream bare paper along the lower-left edge and bottom-left corner, and the books and hearth stopping short of the right edge and bottom-right corner. Holmes wears a plain dark suit and wing collar with slicked-back hair, no costume or prop of a specific screen adaptation, so the likeness claim rests on the face alone; flawed on the agreed lettering (the slip reads 'Missing').

A 5x crop of the bottom-right corner shows the green and brown washes ending at a ragged boundary with a sliver of white paper about 3-8px wide along the lower right edge and corner. Small but really there, and accepted for this item; the grinning clawed Cat on the bough and Alice looking up are right.

A 4x crop of the open strong box on the desk shows two or three more blue gems inside while Holmes holds the one blue stone to the window light, so the single stone is both in his hand and already in the box, multiplied. Small but a real contradiction; the agreed costume rule break and pseudo-script also make it flawed.

In the background group at upper right only the five of hearts is a flat oblong card; the other four (two in pip-marked tunics, a man in green bent over a wire hoop, a man in an orange coat and hat) are ordinary full-bodied humans where the croquet-ground's soldiers and courtiers should be flat cards. Small in the frame but a real break of the card rule.

A bearded man in a dark mantle, the largest figure, leans over scrolls on a stone table addressing a seated group in a Greek town below an acropolis: the letter's author drawn delivering his own words. Nothing of the verse's own image appears, no mirror, dim reflection or face-to-face meeting, so the moment is not shown.

Edge crops show the wave washes ending in rounded ragged boundaries a few pixels short of the left and right edges, leaving a thin irregular white margin that is not foam (near-white is about a third of the outermost columns against about 5 percent twenty pixels in). Accepted for this item; Jesus asleep on the cushion in the stern with a disciple shaking his shoulder is right.

The Mock Turtle and Gryphon rear up either side of Alice on dry shingle, but the sea behind them stands as a see-through green wall up to a waterline under the sky with jellyfish floating at head height inside it, and live coral grows on the dry beach at both sides. The place is at once open-air shore and underwater, a self-contradictory setting.

Four soldiers crouch over a heap of garments, one with an open palm, while on the hill the crucified Jesus still wears a full tunic and blue mantle, so his clothing is both on him and being divided on the ground. Ruled the same way as the other image of this verse.

A 3x crop shows Peter in the left foreground with hand to chest, but the bound Jesus stands with his back to Peter and his head in profile facing right toward the fire. The Lord turning and looking at Peter, the action that defines the verse, is not shown, though the people and courtyard are right.

Holmes at left closes the slide of the dark lantern, bareheaded in a plain black frock coat and wing collar with slicked-back hair; no costume, hairpiece or prop reproduces a specific screen adaptation, and the likeness claim rests on the gaunt face alone. Vault, crates, Watson's revolver, Jones and Merryweather are as narrated, with no lettering and paint to all edges.

A 5x crop of the bottom-left corner shows the green grass washes ending in a ragged boundary that leaves a wedge of white paper about 15-20px into the corner and up the lower left edge. Small but really there and accepted; the item is flawed only on the agreed card-pip lettering.

The foreground man in a rough cloak with a staff stands back to the viewer watching the throne: the seer witnessing his own vision, not shown speaking or writing the passage, so the context involves him. The four eyed winged creatures, glassy sea, crowned elders and a throne holding only mist and drapery all belong to the moment.

A 3x crop of the stacked crates at the far right shows a small pasted label on the second crate down (about x 1320-1350, y 240-265) carrying two rows of squiggle pseudo-script, unreadable but a writing-like inscription. The image is fully judgeable, so the verdict is flawed rather than uncertain; bare paper at the top-left is accepted.

Besides the King pointing from the bench in crown, judge's wig and white beard, a second crowned, wigged, white-bearded king with a heart-pip card body stands large in the lower-right foreground, a duplicate the passage does not call for. Ruled the same way as the doubled king in the lions' den image; the hat-tag scribble is the agreed lettering.

The top edge is a pale blue-grey tinted wash, not bare paper, but along the right edge (about y 130-195) the cloud washes end at a pigment line 4-6px short of the edge with near-white paper beyond, and near-white is absent twenty pixels in. A small sliver, accepted for this item; Jesus standing with arm out over a calming sea is right.

6x and 20x crops of the cross show the small white plaque carrying a faint row of grey dabs across its middle, a suggested inscription that is tiny and unreadable but present. Jesus hangs on the cross fully dressed in a long tunic and blue mantle while the soldiers divide his garments below, the same contradiction as in the other image of this verse.

Two elders, one with a staff and one in a priest's breastplate, stand in the camp looking up at the cloud of light over the tabernacle: they are shown receiving the speech, the 'you' the law addresses, not delivering or writing it. The failure is the missing pig, carried by the agreed scene_mismatch.
